verdicts.title: disable_user lacks the last-admin guard that delete_user has, and no re-enable route exists — an admin can irreversibly brick all admin capability
verdicts.reason: Code-truth confirmed: disable_user (admin.rs:68-80) checks only that the user exists, then unconditionally calls db.disable_user(*id) and revoke_all_sessions_for_user(*id) with no admin-count check. Sibling delete_user (admin.rs:98-120) does have the exact guard (role.is_admin() && count_active_admins() <= 1 => Conflict), confirming the asymmetry is real and not an intentional design choice reflected elsewhere in this file. This file also defines no enable/re-enable endpoint alongside list_users/create_user/disable_user/reset_user_password/delete_user, so nothing in the cited source contradicts the claim.
